site.name: LINTHESIS
site.intro: I'm Mi Lin (Liam). I started in data science, machine learning and statistics, and now care most about AI, blockchain, software, business and startups. I like to write and to share, and to turn ideas into things: software, books, and a few experiments still in progress. This is where they live.

projects.title: Lookbook
projects.sub: A visual index of design systems
projects.one_liner: Over 80 design systems from well-known products, rendered as pages you can browse, compare and take away.

feature.problem: A design system is usually just a document: colors, type, radii and components described in prose. It is hard to see what it feels like in use, and harder still to compare a few of them. Lookbook renders those specs as pages, then turns them into formats you can copy into a project.

Drop the CSS variables or Tailwind config into your own project
Import into Figma's Tokens Studio (W3C Design Tokens JSON)
Keep DESIGN.md in the project root so your coding assistant can always refer to it
tech: Each design system is one DESIGN.md; categories and summaries live in CATALOG.md, which drives the cards and filters.
One sample landing page rendered from each set of design tokens, so the systems are actually comparable.
Vite and plain JavaScript, output as a static site.
Formats are bundled into a .zip in the browser, with no backend.
Automated tests cover data parsing, every page render, export formats and text contrast; GitHub Actions deploys on push to main.

projects.intro: Each design system lives in a single DESIGN.md: colors, type, radii, spacing and components. Lookbook renders the same sample page from those tokens, so you can see what Stripe, Linear or Notion feel like without reading the spec.
features: Browse: grouped by category, searchable in Chinese or English, filterable by dark or light
Preview: every template rendered as a complete sample landing page
Inspect: palette, type scale, radii and spacing, and every component definition
Compare: put two design systems side by side, or draw two at random
Export: AI prompts, CSS variables, Tailwind config and more, bundled in one click

related: Also a local-first macOS app: no online service needed, and data stays on the machine.
Aide lets a local model call desktop tools; this guide covers giving an agent a tool system.
projects.title: Aide
projects.sub: A local AI entry point for the desktop
projects.one_liner: Press ⌘⌃L and say what you want, or select text first. Local Ollama models, nothing uploaded.
projects.intro: A SwiftUI / AppKit shell around a headless Python core. A hotkey opens the Quick Panel, which runs requests with local desktop tools. Selected text can be translated, explained, summarized or rewritten, and a screenshot region opens a new chat with the image attached. Anything that changes data asks for confirmation first.
features: Quick Panel: ⌘⌃L runs a request with local desktop tools
Pick an action for selected text, or type your own instruction
⌘⌃S captures a region into a new chat
Workspace: chat history and search, streaming Markdown, regenerate
Changes show the exact action and run only after you confirm
projects.note: Not notarized yet: on first launch macOS blocks it, and you open it once from System Settings → Privacy & Security.

related: It generates AI research reports automatically, and research reports are one starting point of the Research2Video workflow.
Research2Video turns material into a script; this project breaks the implicit thinking in writing into checkable steps.
Also a local workbench: Atlas for a library, this one for research to finished video.
projects.title: Research2Video
projects.sub: 研映 · From research to video
projects.one_liner: A local workflow from research and drafting through voice-over, visuals, subtitles and video to publishing.
projects.intro: Two modules. The research console handles research tasks, sources, scheduling, script recipes and the video workflow. AutoVideo handles voice-over, visual planning, Remotion rendering, subtitles, intros and outros, and final delivery.
features: Research tasks, sources and scheduled runs
Script recipes and a management console for the video workflow
Voice-over, visual planning, subtitles, intros and outros
Remotion rendering, final delivery and publishing management

related: The same idea of a browsable library, for design systems.
Atlas's template factory hands a dev pack to AI to implement; this guide covers going from need to prompt to product.
A dev pack is handed to AI to implement and verify; this online book is about steering Codex toward verifiable results.
projects.title: Application Atlas
projects.sub: A library of software application types
projects.one_liner: A library and local workbench covering 1,805 software types across 29 top-level domains.
projects.intro: The English entries are the source of truth, backed by research notes, a category tree and persisted translations. On top sits a template factory that exports a standard development pack from a scenario template, hands it to an AI to implement, and verifies the browser journeys.
features: 1,805 types, 29 domains, 270 directory nodes, 33 product instances
Formal English entries with matching research notes and boundaries
Local drafts API and a React workbench
Template factory with trial scenarios such as bookmarks, personal budget and meeting notes

projects.title: PersonalSpace
projects.sub: A native macOS personal digital space
projects.one_liner: A local-first personal library: read-only access to folders you authorize, search and preview, and reminders for what needs doing.
projects.intro: A native macOS app with no server, account or online API. Scanning is read-only, managed copies are copies rather than moves, and there is no way to delete source files. Manual workflows keep working when no model is available. Milestones M1–M10 are implemented locally.
features: Native file library with persistent folder authorization
Search and system preview
Personal objects, links and managed copies
Four kinds of matters with on-demand recognition, fact checking, to-dos and local system reminders
Sensitive markers, backup and restore, quick capture
projects.note: This is currently a local, ad hoc signed development build. It has not been signed with a Developer ID or notarized.

projects.title: Radar
projects.one_liner: Describe what to follow in plain language, collect on a schedule, and get events that link back to the source.
projects.intro: From a plain-language watch, Radar finds and trial-reads sources, collects periodically, keeps a baseline and removes duplicates, then reports events with links to the original. No API key is needed. A new watch only records a baseline; only later content raises alerts.
features: Four collectors: GitHub Releases, GitHub repo discovery, RSS / Atom, static HTML
Source trial reads and confirmation, feed auto-discovery, CSS selector preview
Unique event keys for dedup, ETag / 304, rate limits and network errors tracked per source
Menu bar, system notifications, in-process timer with catch-up on wake
12 automated tests passing

print_books.title: Deep Dive into Data Analysis with R
print_books.sub: 深入浅出R语言数据分析
print_books.intro: Covers data analysis methods and common models, then works through case studies in R: data acquisition and web scraping, preprocessing and exploration, survival analysis, principal component analysis, linear and logistic regression, clustering, association rules, random forests, support vector machines, neural networks, text mining and social network analysis. Written for beginner and advanced R users and for data science practitioners.

print_books.title: Data Visualization with R in Practice
print_books.intro: A multi-angle guide to data visualization in R, with more than 500 worked examples covering over 30 families of statistical graphics.

print_books.title: Statistical Analysis with R in Practice
print_books.intro: Application-first coverage of commonly used R packages and the implementation of statistical methods and statistical machine learning models. Eleven chapters in four parts: R basics, statistical analysis, applications (business A/B testing, marketing analytics, credit scoring), and reproducible research with Shiny visualization.

print_books.title: Getting Started with SPSS and Data Analysis in Practice
print_books.intro: Step-by-step illustrated operations, guidance on statistical thinking, learning by doing through cases, and companion videos and materials.

ebooks.title: Mastering Codex
ebooks.sub: 驾驭 Codex · Not just using it, but steering it
ebooks.intro: Turn vague ideas into verifiable results. Understand what it does, keep your own judgment, and find your way back when it goes wrong. Eight progressive parts, 28 chapters, 7 kinds of interactive learning and 5 kinds of practical tasks.

ebooks.title: Mastering Claude
ebooks.sub: 驾驭 Claude · Not just asking, but getting it done
ebooks.intro: From first opening Claude Code Desktop to organizing complex projects, spotting wrong assumptions and verifying real deliverables. Planned as 8 parts and 32 chapters; 2 sample chapters are open now. An unofficial, independent educational project.

ebooks.title: LLM Inference Engineering in Practice
ebooks.sub: 大模型 Inference 工程实践 · From model files to a working service
ebooks.intro: Start with a small model, not a big one, and build the full range of inference engineering through experiments. Each chapter is tied to a real experiment and its run evidence. Covers prefill, decode, TTFT, TPOT, throughput, quantization, caching and concurrency.

writing_featured.desc: Language that serves thinking, expression, collaboration and action: seven principles, four models, and operators you can apply directly.
How to design, build, debug, evaluate and productionize agent systems, understanding the mechanics without leaning on framework abstractions.
From a first API call to tools, memory, RAG, multi-agent collaboration and evaluation, in 12 chapters.
Part one builds the tokenizer, transformer and pretraining from scratch; part two is hands-on fine-tuning.
Building personal tools with AI: from turning a need into a prompt to setup, UI, databases and backend APIs.
The opening of this series: why code is not the system, and what a missing system blueprint costs.
Treating the self as an object of knowledge: why it is hard to see, and how desire, fear and need serve as evidence of it.
From what A/B testing is for and where it applies, to the statistics behind it: normal, binomial and beta distributions.

lab: A local-first learning workspace that turns a topic or a set of sources into a learning artifact: goal → main process → stage → concept × operation.
A local-first AI research app: give it a goal, and it finds real resources, matches them one by one, and returns traceable candidate paths.
A structured-judgment engine that helps people think through important real-world decisions in guided conversation.
The full system for cognitive language engineering, currently v0.7, with the learning path Principle → Model → interface → operator → language pattern.
A research LLM writing system and its desktop workbench, turning the tacit cognition of writing into steps you can inspect.
An automated AI research report generator with a web console: define jobs in YAML and an agent searches and writes the report.
